nodes.description: Pathogenic variants in a gene encoding one of the phosphorylase kinase (PhK) subunits reduce or abolish holoenzyme activity. PhK is a heterotetramer of four copies each of an alpha, beta, gamma and delta subunit; the gamma subunit carries the catalytic site and the alpha, beta and delta (calmodulin) subunits regulate it. Tissue-specific isoforms mean the resulting deficiency is confined to liver, to muscle, or to both, depending on which subunit gene is affected.

evidence.snippet: The phosphorylase kinase holoenzyme is made up of four copies of each of four subunits (alpha, beta, gamma and delta). The liver isoforms of the alpha-, beta- and gamma-subunits are encoded by PHKA2, PHKB and PHKG2, respectively.
